tone: You are writing the words for the website of AMDL, an open-source, self-hosted tool that downloads music from Apple Music to the user's own disk as finished, tagged files.

Restrained and plain. Say what the thing does, in the fewest words that are true. No hype, no superlatives ("best", "ultimate", "blazing", "seamless", "powerful", "effortless"), no exclamation marks (neither ! nor ！), no rhetorical questions in body text, no emoji.

Short. Every key has two hard limits in characters: maxChars for en.json and maxCharsZh for zh-CN.json. Only visible text counts: [text](href) counts as its text, and the ` and ** marks themselves do not count.

Concrete. Prefer a fact (a format, a number, a command) to an adjective. Use only the facts listed for each key (the facts object holds their text); do not add claims. Numbers and names exactly as given.
Strings a key lists in verbatim must appear exactly so, in both languages.
Calm second person ("you") where a subject is needed; no "we".
Unreleased things are said to be coming or in development, never as available.
Never name or imply endorsement by Apple. "Apple Music" is the service the user already pays for.
Headings: sentence case, no final period. Body: full sentences with periods. Button and link labels: two or three words, a verb first where natural, no period.

Marks: a key may use only the marks its marks list names: code as `text` for commands, paths, addresses and config keys; strong as **text** (the one highlighted phrase in hero.lead, UI labels in the Docker steps); link as [text](href), where href is one of the key's links.

Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) is written for Chinese readers, not translated word for word: natural, plain Mandarin as in good Chinese technical docs. Full-width punctuation (，。：；（）), a half-width space between Chinese and Latin letters or digits (下载 ALAC 24-bit), product and format names left in Latin (AMDL, Apple Music, ALAC, AAC, Docker, MCP; Dolby Atmos may be 杜比全景声), commands and UI labels of the apps unchanged (the apps are in English).
Keys with "lang": "other" are written in the other language in each file: ui.otherLang is 中文 in en.json and English in zh-CN.json; ui.otherLangLabel is Chinese in en.json and English in zh-CN.json.
Accessibility labels (keys ending in label, Label or Alt, or under ui.) describe what a screen reader user would otherwise miss, in one plain sentence, no "image of".

facts.F01: AMDL (`amdl`) downloads music from Apple Music to your own disk: it resolves a link, downloads the encrypted media, decrypts it, remuxes and tags it, and saves finished `.m4a` files
facts.F02: It takes song, album, playlist, artist and radio station links, or a search of the catalog. Up to 100 links at once
facts.F03: Self-hosted, for one person: each install serves one user; there are no user accounts and no auth (access control belongs to whatever runs in front)
facts.F04: It needs your own Apple Music subscription
facts.F05: It needs a wrapper: the service that holds your Apple Music login. amdl holds no Apple account and no keys
facts.F06: Decryption runs inside amdl, in-process (a pure-Go translation of Temari, MIT)
facts.F07: No decrypted copy of a whole track is written to disk: decrypted samples are piped straight into ffmpeg
facts.F08: Catalog reads use Apple's undocumented web-player API, which can change without notice; no Apple developer key is needed
facts.F09: Audio only: music videos are not supported; live radio such as Apple Music 1 is not supported; a station is a rolling list of what Apple offers now
facts.F12: 2.0 is in development (release candidates; rc.13 is the last) [unreleased]
facts.F13: Codecs, in a priority list you order: `alac` (Apple Lossless), `ec3` (Dolby Digital Plus / Dolby Atmos), `ac3` (Dolby Digital), `aac`, `aac-binaural`, `aac-downmix`. AAC-LC is always appended as the last fallback and is not listed
facts.F14: Default priority `["alac"]`. With `codec_alternative` on (default), a codec that runs out of attempts hands over to the next; each codec has its own attempts
facts.F15: ALAC up to 24-bit / 192 kHz by default; a lower ceiling can be set. Apple serves ALAC at 44.1 kHz and above, 16- and 24-bit
facts.F16: The apps label qualities `ALAC 24/96`, `Atmos`, `Dolby Digital`, `AAC 256`, `AAC Binaural`, `AAC Downmix`; the long form is `ALAC 24-bit · 96 kHz`. AAC is 256 kbps
facts.F17: Cover art is embedded, 5000×5000 JPEG by default; album and playlist covers are also saved as `cover.jpg` next to the music, and the artist's picture as `artist.jpg` in the artist folder (when Apple has one)
facts.F18: Lyrics are embedded as LRC, timed by line or by word; translation and pronunciation (romanization) can be added; `.lrc` or `.ttml` files can be saved beside the track
facts.F19: Each track is checked for integrity after download (on by default)
facts.F20: Songs, albums and artists share one folder tree: `library/{AlbumArtist}/{AlbumName}/{SongNumber:02d}. {SongName}` by default; playlists go to `playlists/{PlaylistName}/…` and stations to `stations/{StationName}/…`. The templates are configurable
facts.F21: A file already at its path is adopted, not downloaded again (unless `download.overwrite_existing` is on); downloading again replaces a file only once the new one is complete
facts.F22: One binary, `amdl`: the command line, the MCP server, the terminal interface and the backend with its web console
facts.F23: Desktop app: native, for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux (amd64; needs GTK 3); attached to each release as `.dmg`, setup `.exe`, `.deb` and `.tar.gz`. Packages are not signed yet: macOS and Windows each stop the first launch once
facts.F24: The desktop app is a client of an AMDL server, or standalone with the backend inside the app; standalone it shares one backend and history with `amdl service` on the same machine. On first launch it asks where downloads run, and its setup screen installs ffmpeg, QEMU where needed and the wrapper
facts.F25: Web console: the browser client the server serves at `/console/` on the API's port, with nothing to install on the device that opens it; it uses only the public API. Light and dark. The Docker image publishes it on port 18080 for the network. A binary install stays on this machine (loopback): `amdl serve` on port 18080, `amdl service install` on a port it picks at install (`amdl service status` prints the address). Never write the loopback IP address on the page (the build rejects it); say "this machine"
facts.F26: The console's pages: New download, Overview, Activity, Library (your Apple Music library, when switched on), Settings, Logs; a command palette and keyboard shortcuts; a phone layout with bottom tabs
facts.F27: Terminal UI: `amdl` with no arguments (or `amdl tui`); prints into the terminal's scrollback; paste a link or type to search; up to three jobs as cards with an album bar and each track's stage; `/` commands such as `/quality`, `/queue`, `/library`, `/jobs`, `/retry`, `/logs`, `/login`, `/help`; follows a light or dark terminal; with `NO_COLOR` the bars still read by shape
facts.F28: Command line: every result is JSON on stdout, errors are JSON on stderr with an exit status per kind of failure; `amdl cli search "<task>"` finds the command for a task; `--dry-run` on changes
facts.F29: MCP: `amdl mcp` serves 37 tools over stdio; `amdl cli setup` prints the config for Claude Code, Codex or any `mcpServers` client and an agent skill; no tool signs the wrapper in, so an Apple ID password never passes through a model
facts.F30: An agent goes from a search to a download in two calls (`search_catalog`, then `start_download`) and follows the job with `wait_for_job`
facts.F31: HTTP API: REST and Server-Sent Events under `/api/v1` on the console's port; the OpenAPI spec is `internal/api/openapi.yaml`; no CORS headers (the console is its only browser client)
facts.F32: Hooks: a webhook or a command when a job is queued, finishes, fails or is cancelled. Presets: ntfy, Bark and Telegram notifications; Plex, Jellyfin and Emby library refreshes; Custom. Commands are edited only in the file. Off by default
facts.F33: Docker: the image `ghcr.io/amdl-web/apple-music-downloader` for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, with ffmpeg inside, on port 18080; the Compose file is `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, which carries the wrapper-manager service commented out; `PUID`/`PGID` default 1000:1000
facts.F34: Binary install: `install.sh` (macOS, Linux) checks the release against `SHA256SUMS` and installs `amdl` into `~/.local/bin`; `install.ps1` (Windows) into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\amdl`. Releases build macOS and Linux for amd64 and arm64 and Windows for amd64; Windows on ARM runs the amd64 build under emulation
facts.F35: Homebrew and Scoop packages arrive with 2.0.1 [unreleased]
facts.F36: ffmpeg 8 or later; `amdl doctor` checks the server, ffmpeg, the wrapper and the service and prints the command that installs what is missing
facts.F37: `amdl wrapper install` gets a wrapper (wrapper-manager, checked against a pinned hash) and runs it natively on Linux x86_64 with user namespaces, in a QEMU guest elsewhere; not on Windows on ARM
facts.F38: `amdl service install` runs the backend as a service that starts at login (LaunchAgent, systemd user unit or Task Scheduler task); `amdl service status` prints the console's address. With a wrapper on another machine, pass its address: `amdl service install --wrapper <url>`. The wrapper is signed in on the console's Account page, with the terminal UI's `/login`, or with `amdl wrapper login`
facts.F39: The wrapper's native and Docker launchers (the Compose file's wrapper-manager service included) run on Linux x86_64 (amd64) and need user namespaces (`unshare -Ur true` must succeed); on arm64, or on a host without user namespaces such as Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant, which needs `/dev/kvm`
facts.F40: wrapper-manager v2 holds up to 10 Apple Music accounts and has the login the console's Account page uses (two-step codes are asked for there)
facts.F41: Docker sign-in: open `http://localhost:18080/`, Settings › Account, set Session service to `http://wrapper-manager:8080`, save and restart from the notice, sign in with the Apple ID, paste a link into New download; files land in `./data/downloads`
facts.F42: Binary installs save music to `~/Music/AMDL` (`%UserProfile%\Music\AMDL` on Windows)
facts.F43: Until 2.0.0 is released, the install script and the `latest` image mean an older release: pass a 2.0 release candidate's tag with `--version` (`-Version` on Windows), for example `v2.0.0-rc.13`, and in the Compose file replace `latest` with the same version without the `v` (`2.0.0-rc.13`; images are tagged without it). A database written by rc.1 to rc.7 cannot be opened [unreleased: removed on release day]
facts.F44: Coming from 1.x: the database migrates on first start and 1.x cannot read it afterwards; back it up and read the upgrade guide first
facts.F45: The apps are in English; this site and the README are in English and Simplified Chinese

meta.title.purpose: Browser tab and search result title. Product name, then what it does.

meta.description.purpose: Search snippet and social card text: what it is, what it saves, the ways to use it.

meta.ogAlt.purpose: Alt text of the social card image (the hero headline beside three album covers).

ui.skip.purpose: Skip link to the main content.

ui.nav.purpose: Accessible name of the header navigation.

ui.sections.purpose: Label of the header menu that lists the page's sections.

ui.anchor.purpose: Accessible name of the small link glyph after each section title (a link to this section).

ui.theme.purpose: Accessible name of the light/dark/system switch.

ui.github.purpose: Accessible name of the GitHub icon link.

ui.otherLang.purpose: The other language's own name, shown as the language link. In en.json write 中文; in zh-CN.json write English.

ui.otherLangLabel.purpose: Tooltip of the language link, written in the OTHER language (en.json: Chinese; zh-CN.json: English).

ui.copy.purpose: Accessible name of a code block's copy button.

ui.home.purpose: Accessible name of the logo link to the page top.

ui.prev.purpose: Accessible name of the stepper's previous arrow.

ui.next.purpose: Accessible name of the stepper's next arrow.

nav.how.purpose: Menu entry for section 1 (from a link to a file).

nav.apps.purpose: Menu entry for section 3 (desktop app, web console, terminal, agents).

header.install.purpose: The header's primary button, jumps to the install section.

hero.prereleaseBadge.purpose: Temporary first part of the eyebrow pill: AMDL 2.0 is in development. Deleted with its markup on release day.

hero.eyebrow.purpose: Permanent part of the small pill above the headline: two plain facts that stay true after release (for example self-hosted and open source). No version state; that is hero.prereleaseBadge.

hero.title.purpose: The headline, two lines separated by \n. Line 1 names the service, line 2 (shown in the accent color) says where the music ends up. Each line at most 28 characters.

hero.lead.purpose: One or two sentences under the shelf of album covers: what goes in, what comes out, how it is used. Contains exactly one **highlighted** phrase (the outcome).

hero.source.purpose: Small text link at the end of the Runs-on row, after the platform names: opens the GitHub repository (for example 'View source'). The hero has no buttons.

hero.runsOn.purpose: Label before the platform names macOS, Windows, Linux, Docker.

hero.shelfLabel.purpose: Accessible description of the hero picture: made-up album covers on a shelf and the finished file 01. Glass Weather.m4a in ALAC 24-bit · 96 kHz. Name no number of covers: the wide shelf shows five, a phone three.

how.title.purpose: Section 1 heading: a link becomes a file.

how.lead.purpose: One sentence under the heading: what AMDL does with a link, and that the decryption happens on your machine.

how.link.title.purpose: Card A title: the input (a link).

how.link.text.purpose: Card A sentence: which links are accepted, or search instead. A demo album link is shown under it.

how.link.note.purpose: Card A bottom line, bold: a short plain statement about the input (for example that many links can go at once).

how.amdl.title.purpose: Card B title: what AMDL does (may simply be AMDL or a short verb phrase).

how.amdl.steps.0.text.purpose: Step 1 clause: fetches the encrypted media from Apple.

how.amdl.steps.1.text.purpose: Step 2 clause: inside amdl, with keys from your own wrapper.

how.amdl.steps.2.text.purpose: Step 3 clause: ffmpeg writes the .m4a; no decrypted whole track on disk.

how.amdl.steps.3.text.purpose: Step 4 clause: tags, cover and lyrics go into the file, then an integrity check.

how.amdl.note.purpose: Card B bottom line, bold: one plain statement (for example that a failed codec falls back to the next).

how.file.title.purpose: Card C title: the output on your disk.

how.file.text.purpose: Card C sentence: songs, albums and artists share one folder tree; a folder tree is shown under it.

how.file.note.purpose: Card C bottom line, bold: files already there are kept, not downloaded again.

how.label.purpose: Accessible description of the folder tree in card C: under library/, the artist folder Mira Solenne holds artist.jpg and the album folder Glass Weather, which holds the numbered .m4a tracks and cover.jpg.

how.more.purpose: Soft button to the download pipeline documentation.

formats.lead.purpose: One sentence: lossless up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos or AAC, in the order you choose.

formats.file.codec.purpose: Row label in the file facts: codec / quality.

formats.file.cover.purpose: Row label: cover art (value shown is 5000 × 5000).

formats.file.lyricsValue.purpose: Row value: LRC, timed by line or by word. May use `LRC`.

formats.file.tagsValue.purpose: Row value: what the tags hold (title, artist, album, track number and so on), very short.

formats.ladder.head.purpose: Small heading over the codec ladder: tried in this order.

formats.rows.alac.purpose: Note under ALAC: lossless, up to 24-bit / 192 kHz.

formats.rows.ec3.purpose: Note under Dolby Atmos: spatial audio, where the album has it.

formats.rows.aaclc.purpose: Note under AAC-LC: always tried last, not listed.

formats.also.purpose: Label before three extra codec names (ac3, aac-binaural, aac-downmix): also available.

formats.caption.purpose: Caption under the card: what quality_priority is and that a codec that fails hands over to the next.

apps.title.purpose: Section 3 heading: the ways to use AMDL.

apps.lead.purpose: One or two sentences: one backend, several front ends, use whichever fits.

apps.shown.purpose: Small note under the stepper: these are illustrations of the real screens with made-up music, in English like the apps.

apps.more.purpose: Short label before the two text links (HTTP API, hooks) under the apps section, for example 'Also:'.

apps.desktop.caption.purpose: The panel's one or two sentences under the mock: a native app for macOS, Windows and Linux; a client of your server, or standalone with the backend inside, setting up ffmpeg and the wrapper for you.

apps.desktop.doc.purpose: Button to the desktop install guide.

apps.desktop.label.purpose: Accessible description of the mock: the desktop app's album page, Glass Weather mid-download, five of twelve tracks saved, the folder it saves to.

apps.console.caption.purpose: The panel's one or two sentences: the server's own page, opened in a browser, with nothing to install on the device: from any device on the network when the server runs on a NAS or in Docker (port 18080), on this machine for a local install.

apps.console.doc.purpose: Button to the web console section of the README.

apps.console.label.purpose: Accessible description: the console's Overview, one failed link under Needs attention, three albums downloading as cards in their cover colors, one queued link.

apps.terminal.caption.purpose: The panel's one or two sentences: `amdl` with no arguments opens an interactive terminal UI (paste a link or search; jobs show each track's stage); every command also prints JSON for scripts.

apps.terminal.doc.purpose: Button to the terminal interface docs.

apps.terminal.label.purpose: Accessible description: the terminal UI with the banner, Glass Weather downloading track by track, the prompt, and search results for Mira Solenne.

apps.agents.caption.purpose: The panel's one or two sentences: `amdl mcp` gives AI agents 37 tools, from a search to a finished download; no tool signs in, so an Apple ID password never passes through a model.

apps.agents.label.purpose: Accessible description of the chat: the user asks for the new Nightjar Coast album in Dolby Atmos; the agent calls search_catalog, start_download and wait_for_job, then says where the 11 tracks were saved.

apps.agents.chat.you.purpose: Speaker label of the user's message.

apps.agents.chat.agent.purpose: Speaker label of the agent's reply.

apps.agents.chat.ask.purpose: The user's request in the chat, natural and short: download the new Nightjar Coast album in Dolby Atmos. Keep the artist name Nightjar Coast verbatim.

apps.agents.chat.reply.purpose: The agent's reply: done, Low Tide Signals (2026), all 11 tracks in Dolby Atmos, saved to the folder. Must contain `/volume1/music/library/Nightjar Coast/Low Tide Signals/` verbatim in a code mark and the album name verbatim.

apps.agents.tools.purpose: Summary line of the expandable list (closed by default) of all 37 MCP tools.

apps.agents.groups.catalog.purpose: Tool group name: catalog (search, albums, playlists, links, quality).

apps.agents.groups.jobs.purpose: Tool group name: jobs (downloads in the queue).

apps.agents.groups.library.purpose: Tool group name: records of what was downloaded.

apps.agents.groups.apple.purpose: Tool group name: your Apple Music library.

apps.agents.groups.system.purpose: Tool group name: server and accounts.

apps.agents.config.purpose: Label above the mcpServers JSON: the client config amdl cli setup prints.

apps.api.link.purpose: Text link to the API reference, naming the HTTP API (REST and Server-Sent Events).

apps.hooks.link.purpose: Text link to the hooks documentation, naming hooks (a webhook or a command when a job finishes or fails).

install.lead.purpose: One or two sentences: what you need (an Apple Music subscription and a wrapper, the service that holds your Apple Music login) and the two ways to install.

install.tabsLabel.purpose: Accessible name of the Binary/Docker switch: how to install.

install.binary.steps.0.text.purpose: Step 1 text: the script checks SHA256SUMS and installs into ~/.local/bin (a user programs folder on Windows).

install.binary.steps.1.text.purpose: Step 2 text: every track goes through ffmpeg 8 or later; amdl doctor says whether it is there and prints the install command.

install.binary.steps.2.text.purpose: Step 3 text: native on Linux x86_64, in a QEMU guest elsewhere; skip it if a wrapper already runs on a NAS or server.

install.binary.steps.3.text.purpose: Step 4 text: runs the backend as a service that starts at login; `amdl service status` prints the console's address; sign the wrapper in there or with `amdl wrapper login`. For a wrapper on another machine, add `--wrapper <its address>` to `amdl service install`.

install.docker.steps.0.title.purpose: Step 1 title: get the Compose file.

install.docker.steps.0.text.purpose: Step 1 text: in an empty directory; create data/downloads first and give it to the backend's user (PUID:PGID, 1000:1000 by default).

install.docker.steps.1.title.purpose: Step 2 title: turn on the wrapper.

install.docker.steps.1.text.purpose: Step 2 text: in docker-compose.yml, uncomment the wrapper-manager service and the volumes: block at the end.

install.docker.steps.2.text.purpose: Step 3 text: Compose builds wrapper-manager from AMDL-Web's wrapper fork, so the host needs internet access.

install.docker.steps.3.title.purpose: Step 4 title: point at the wrapper and sign in.

install.docker.steps.3.text.purpose: Step 4 text, before the address block: open http://localhost:18080/, go to Settings › Account and set Session service to the address below, then save and restart from the notice. Addresses in `code`, UI labels in **bold**.

install.docker.steps.3.after.purpose: Step 4 text, after the address block: sign in with your Apple ID and paste a link into New download; finished files land in ./data/downloads. Paths in `code`, UI labels in **bold**.

install.prereleaseLabel.purpose: Label pill of the 2.0 note, for example the version number with a word for 'note'.

install.prerelease.purpose: The 2.0 note (removed on release day): until 2.0.0 is released, pass a release candidate's tag to the install script with --version (-Version on Windows), for example v2.0.0-rc.13, and in the Compose file replace latest with the same version without the v (2.0.0-rc.13); Homebrew and Scoop arrive with 2.0.1; a database from rc.1 to rc.7 cannot be opened.

install.nas.label.purpose: Label pill of the NAS note.

install.nas.text.purpose: NAS note: the wrapper needs Linux x86_64 with user namespaces (unshare -Ur true must succeed); on arm64, or on a host without user namespaces such as Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant, which needs /dev/kvm.

install.nas.link.purpose: Link label to the wrapper setup docs.

install.more.purpose: Closing line: every option is in the install guide and the deployment guide; coming from 1.x, read the 2.0 upgrade guide first. Use exactly the three links in `links`, one each, in that order.

cta.title.purpose: Big headline of the closing band: an invitation to start, plain.

cta.button.purpose: Its one button, to the install guide.

footer.tagline.purpose: One line under the footer logo: what AMDL is.

footer.notice.purpose: The notice: needs your own Apple Music subscription, for personal use (one install serves one person), relies on Apple's undocumented web-player API which can change without notice.

footer.legal.purpose: Bottom line: open source under AGPL-3.0, and that AMDL is not affiliated with Apple.
